blocks.why: Lights out at 20:30 local even though it feels ridiculous — the alarm goes at 04:25 for an 06:10 report and there is no second chance at this sleep.
Home by 18:00, straight to bed after eating, because tomorrow is another 05:05 report and I only have about ten hours behind the front door.
This afternoon block is my main sleep for the all-nighter — blackout blinds, phone off, treat 13:30 like midnight.
Post-night recovery sleep straight after the ARN/CDG round-robin, and it has to be finished by 15:30 to make the 19:10 report.
Short night after a midnight landing — get what I can before a twelve-hour duty with a 10:50 report.
First proper night of the month with a day off behind it — sleep it out, no alarm.
Banking sleep on the day off ahead of a 05:40 report and a near fourteen-hour duty tomorrow.
Early to bed on a day off is the only way to be worth anything at 05:40 report with four sectors to ARN and back twice.
Long recovery night after a 13h53 duty — the 15:25 report tomorrow means I can actually take it.
Nap before signing on, because this one doesn't get me back on stand until nearly 03:00 local.
Straight to bed off the BCN night sector — day off means I can sleep through the morning.
Second sleep of the day off, going down early to re-anchor for the 05:05 report — no nap this afternoon, I want the sleep pressure.
Quick top-up after a four-sector day that started at 03:20 wake-up, so I'm not wrecked by the evening.
Full night before the SIM — this is the last decent sleep I'll get for three days, so protect it.
Bed at 17:45 local the moment I'm out of the box, because report is 02:00 local and this evening sleep is all there is.
Afternoon block is the main sleep for tonight's all-nighter — I've already been up through one WOCL and I'm about to do another.
Get the edge off after thirteen hours through the night, but set an alarm — I don't want to wipe out tonight's sleep.
First night of the four days off — back onto local nights properly, get outside in the morning light.
Straight normal night on a day off, paying back the debt from the 11th and 12th.
Another clean night at home — nothing clever needed.
Deliberately going down an hour later to drift towards tomorrow's late start and 02:00 local finish.
Short nap before a 14:40 report — I'll be flying the ARN night leg back into the WOCL.
Home from the 02:37 local landing and into bed on a day off — sleep as long as it comes.
Small nap to bridge the afternoon so I can still get to bed at 20:00 for the 05:40 report.
Early night ahead of the first of two back-to-back early starts.
Top-up after a 03:55 wake-up, because tomorrow's alarm is twenty minutes earlier again.
Second early in a row — bed before 20:00 local, no exceptions.
Nap off the back of the second early; the 12:20 report tomorrow means I can afford it.
Big catch-up night after two earlies, with a late report tomorrow to take advantage of it.
Normal night, day off tomorrow — start topping up for the twelve-hour FCO day on the 23rd.
Day-off nap to bank a bit of extra before an 06:10 report and nearly thirteen hours of duty.
Down early for the 03:25 alarm ahead of the FRA/FCO four-sector day.
Straight into four days off after a 12h55 duty — sleep until the body's finished.
Ordinary night at home on a day off.
Ordinary night at home on a day off.
Starting to pull the wake-up earlier ahead of the 05:05 report on the 28th.
Afternoon nap on the last day off so the early bedtime tonight doesn't feel impossible.
Bed at 19:30 local for the 05:05 report and a four-sector day out to FRA and DUB.
Short nap after a ten-and-a-half hour duty on an early start, purely to get through the evening.
Sleeping in properly — the 13:15 report gives me the room, and tomorrow finishes at 23:37 local.
Home from the late DUB turn and into bed; a 15:25 report tomorrow means I can take a full night.
Last duty done, home by 20:30 — normal night to close the roster out.

conflicts.statement: Two duties on the same calendar day: the LHR–BCN early ends 10:28Z and the all-night ARN/CDG duty reports 20:30Z — 10h02 of rest, of which only about 8h05 is behind my own front door once the 55-minute commute is taken off each end, and all of it in daylight before an 11h37 duty that runs straight through the WOCL.
options: Take the planned 12:30–17:30Z afternoon sleep seriously — blackout blinds, earplugs, phone off, treat 13:30 local as midnight
Ask crewing to drop the 03 SEP early (LY406/LY858) and keep only the night duty
Ask for the night duty to be given to another crew and keep the early
If the afternoon sleep does not happen, call fatigued before report rather than after the first sector

conflicts.statement: The 03 SEP night duty operates LY798, LY422 and LY763 between 00:49Z and 07:37Z — the entire 01:00–05:00Z body-clock low is flown, with three sectors and two takeoffs inside it.
options: Plan the augmented workload: PF/PM swap by sector and keep the low-point sectors on the more rested pilot
Rostered controlled rest on the ARN–LHR cruise if the company scheme allows it
Flag to the operator that this is a full WOCL crossing on the back of an earlier same-day duty

conflicts.statement: Off duty 08:07Z on 04 SEP after the all-nighter, back on report at 18:10Z the same day — 10h03, and the recovery sleep has to be taken in daylight between roughly 09:30Z and 15:30Z.
options: Protect the 09:30–15:30Z sleep as an absolute priority; no errands, no daylight on the way home
Ask crewing to move the 04 SEP FRA turn to a later crew
Request the 04 SEP duty be dropped entirely given it sits between a night duty and a 12h11 duty on the 5th

conflicts.statement: Off duty 23:50Z on the 4th, report 09:50Z on the 5th — exactly 10h00, giving about 6h50 in bed before a 12h11 four-sector duty to ARN and FRA.
options: Accept the short night and plan a rest-period break at LHR between the ARN and FRA rotations
Ask for the LY368/LY176 FRA pair on the 5th to be removed to shorten the day
Flag the 02–05 SEP block as a cumulative-fatigue sequence, not four unrelated duties

conflicts.statement: 02–05 SEP is four duties in four days chained on roughly 10–12 hour turnarounds, including an all-nighter, totalling around 40 hours of duty with the only real recovery being one day off on the 6th.
options: Ask for a second day off adjacent to the 6th
Ask crewing to break the chain by removing the 04 SEP evening FRA turn
Watch for accumulating sleep debt across the block and report it early rather than at the end

conflicts.statement: 13h53 duty with a 04:40Z report — that is a 03:55 local alarm, so the sleep before it has to start around 20:00 local, and the duty then runs until 18:33Z with four sectors.
options: Take the pre-duty nap on the 6th and go to bed at 20:00 local regardless of how it feels
Ask for the second ARN rotation (LY891/LY377) to be removed to shorten a long duty on an early start
Plan proper breaks on the ground at LHR between rotations, not just aircraft turnarounds

conflicts.statement: The SIM on the 11th ends 15:00Z and the next duty reports 01:00Z on the 12th — 10h00, of which the sleep opportunity is roughly 16:45–23:15Z. That means being asleep by 17:45 local on the back of an eight-hour simulator detail, then reporting at 02:00 local at the very start of the WOCL.
options: This is the single worst transition in the roster — raise it with crewing before the month starts, not on the day
Ask for the SIM to be moved to a morning slot on a day with no duty following, or to the 10th
Ask for the 12 SEP 01:00Z duty to be given to a crew who slept the previous night
If neither moves, treat 16:45Z as lights-out with blackout blinds and be prepared to call fatigued

conflicts.statement: Two duties on 12 SEP: 01:00–11:35Z (10h35, reporting at the start of the WOCL) and then 21:35Z–10:39Z on the 13th (13h04, crossing the entire WOCL again) with only 10h00 between them. That is two consecutive nights of the body-clock low with a daytime sleep as the only recovery, on top of the SIM the day before.
options: Escalate the 11–13 SEP sequence as a block, not as three separate days
Ask crewing to remove one of the two 12 SEP duties
Protect the 12:45–19:15Z afternoon sleep as the primary sleep for the night duty
Expect the worst point of the whole roster to be around 03:00–05:00Z on the 13th between BCN and ARN — brief the crew on it

conflicts.statement: Back-to-back early starts: 04:40Z report on the 19th and 04:05Z on the 20th, meaning a 02:55 local alarm and then a 03:20 local alarm on consecutive days with only the evening of the 19th in between.
options: Take the short nap on the afternoon of the 19th and get to bed by 19:30 local
Ask for the 20 SEP FRA turn to be moved a day later so it does not stack on the 19th
Use the 12:20Z report on the 21st to take a genuine lie-in rather than filling the morning

conflicts.statement: The 17 SEP duty lands at 00:37Z and goes off duty 01:07Z — home around 02:00Z, so the final ARN–LHR sector is flown right into the body-clock low at the end of an 11h27 duty.
options: Take the 11:00–12:15Z pre-duty nap before signing on
Ask for the ARN night rotation to be removed, leaving the CDG turn only
Make sure the 18th stays clear as a day off so the recovery sleep is not cut short

conflicts.statement: The roster does not state the reporting offset in words; I have derived it as 60 minutes before STD from every flight duty on the roster, and taken the SIM report on 11 SEP as the stated 07:00Z start with no offset. If Lyra's actual short-haul offset differs, every reportUtc and every wake time shifts with it.
options: Confirm the reporting offset against the Lyra Ops Manual before using these wake times
If the SIM briefing starts before 07:00Z, move the 11 SEP wake-up earlier and the 10 SEP bedtime with it
